title: sandboxed-plugin-wiring-sketchbook
body:
Status: rough brain-dump / personal scratchpad. Not a final design — trying to capture constraints and a tiny API sketch for local sandboxed plugin wiring (host <-> plugin iframe/process) that can be adopted by the local dev runner and the edge sandbox.

Goals / constraints:
- Plugins must run in a sandboxed process or iframe (untrusted) to limit access to host resources.
- Need a small capability negotiation so host only exposes declared capabilities (fs-read, fs-write, network-proxy, tool-invoke).
- Handshake must be resumable and auditable for later forensics.
- Lightweight telemetry and cost attribution attached to each plugin call.
- Fail-open vs fail-closed: default to fail-closed for sensitive capabilities; allow opt-in dev toggles.
- Support two runtime shapes: in-process shim (dev) and out-of-process helper (prod-like).

High-level flow (sequence):
1) Host spawns plugin process (or creates iframe) with restricted environment.
2) Plugin connects over unix domain socket / postMessage and sends "hello" with manifest sig.
3) Host validates manifest signature + checks allowlist for tenant.
4) Host responds with policy blob (capabilities, timeouts, telemetry-token).
5) Plugin observes policy and acknowledges. Live session starts.
6) All tool calls are proxied via host and tagged.
7) Session closes; host records session manifest + decisions.

ASCII sequence diagram:

Host             Plugin
|                 |
| spawn plugin    |
|---------------> |
|                 |
| listen for sock |
| <---------------| connect: {manifest, sig, ver}
| validate sig    |
| policy := {capabilities: [fs-read], ttl: 45s}
| <---------------| policy-token: xyz
| ack             |
|---------------->| ready
|                 |
| proxy-call      |
|---------------->| (plugin -> host)
| validate call   |
| forward to tool |
|---------------->|
|                 |

Handshake payload example (JSON-as-text in the wire):
hello = {
  \"plugin_id\": \"com.example.summarizer\",
  \"version\": \"0.3.1\",
  \"manifest_digest\": \"sha256:...\",
  \"declared_capabilities\": [\"fs-read\", \"http-proxy\"],
  \"public_key\": \"-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----...\"
}

policy response = {
  \"approved_capabilities\": [\"fs-read\"],
  \"timeouts\": {\"call_timeout_ms\": 5000, \"session_idle_ms\": 600000},
  \"telemetry_token\": \"tkn_abc123\",
  \"audit_log_id\": \"audit-20241105-42\"
}

Notes on verification:
- Manifest verification requires a content-addressed bundle (zip) signed by an author key. Host should maintain a small allowlist per org (local dev can run in permissive mode).
- For privacy, policy blob must not include tenant secrets. Telemetry_token is short-lived bearer that maps to internal credentials.

API surface / wire primitives:
- transport choices: unix socket with JSON-RPC v2, postMessage (iframe), or TCP loopback (dev-only).
- messages: hello, policy, ack, call, call-result, heartbeat, close, error, audit-capture.
- call shape: {id, method, params, attachments_meta, cost_estimate_tokens?} — host can enrich with request-context.

Example JSON-RPC-like envelope (text):
{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":\"c1\",\"method\":\"tool.call\",\"params\":{
  \"tool\":\"web.fetch\",
  \"args\":{\"url\":\"https://example.com/api\"},
  \"context\":{ \"session_id\":\"s-42\", \"telemetry_token\":\"tkn_abc123\" }
}}

Security model options (tradeoffs):
- Capability tokens vs ACL: tokens are simple but need lifecycle; ACLs need stronger management but easier to reason about.
- Syscall filtering (seccomp) + filesystem chroot for process-based sandboxes. Iframe uses CSP & postMessage origin checks.
- Instrument every proxied call with audit id to reconstruct event graph.

Telemetry & cost accounting:
- Host mints telemetry_token tied to tenant+session+policy. Token is short-lived (minutes).
- Each call includes estimated token cost; host can reconcile with actual inference cost on model route.
- Provide per-plugin counters: calls, call_time_ms, bytes_in/out, last_seen. Expose via local /metrics endpoint for the runner.

Operational behaviors / edge cases:
- Plugin crash: host marks session dirty, writes audit entry, optionally restarts depending on policy.
- Network proxy capability: host should allow only outbound connections filtered through a proxy that rewrites host header to avoid internal leaks.
- Long-running calls: enforce cancellable handles. Host returns a cancel handle to plugin; plugin can request cancellation.

Dev ergonomics (local runner):
- Developer flow should be frictionless: --dev-sandbox-permissive to skip signing checks, but still run with seccomp.
- Add a small CLI to pack and sign plugin bundles for local testing: redwood-plugin pack/sign/verify.
- Provide a debug mode that streams audit events to stdout for quick inspection.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want nested capability declarations (capabilities granted only for certain endpoints)? Eg fs-read only under /tmp/plugin-123.
- How to represent rate limits per capability? per-minute tokens? simple quotas?
- Should policy be purely declarative JSON or include a tiny policy language for conditional rules? (lean toward JSON + small expressions for now).
- Where to persist final audit traces so security can run queries (S3 blob vs internal events DB)? Need retention policy.

Action items for next pass:
- Sketch the minimal policy JSON schema and validation rules.
- Write a small reference implementation (node/unix-socket) that performs handshake and demo proxying web.fetch.
- Draft CLI helpers for pack/sign/verify and a permissive dev flag.
- Sync with security for seccomp profile and with infra for telemetry token lifecycle.

Notes-to-self: keep this intentionally minimal — primary value is containing host exposure. Keep plugin API surface tiny and explicit.

Random small idea: incremental capability elevation. Plugin starts with minimal read-only capability; if it demonstrates trusted behavior during a session (low-risk calls), host can warrant a temporary elevation for a single op. Feels complex but useful for UX.

End of scratchbook.
